title: Sets: Subsets, Intervals, Venn Diagrams and Set Operations
seo_title: Sets Class 11 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 1)
standard_text: Sets and their representations; empty, finite, infinite and equal sets; subsets, subsets of the set of real numbers (intervals); Venn diagrams; union, intersection, difference and complement of sets and their properties (summary of the CBSE syllabus)
meta_desc: Class 11 Sets worksheet (NCERT Chapter 1): roster and set-builder form, subsets, power set, intervals, union, intersection, difference, complement and Venn diagrams. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets.
key_sub: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).
body_html:
How it works

  • Roster form lists the elements: {2, 3, 5, 7}. Set-builder form gives the rule: {x : x is a prime less than 10}.
  • B ⊂ A when every element of B is in A. A set with n elements has 2n subsets; the power set P(A) has 2n elements.
  • Intervals: (a, b) leaves out both ends, [a, b] keeps both, [a, b) keeps only a.
  • A ∪ B (in A or B), A ∩ B (in both), A − B (in A but not B), A′ = U − A. De Morgan: (A ∪ B)′ = A′ ∩ B′.
Example

A = {1, 2, 3}. How many subsets does A have?

φ, {1}, {2}, {3}, {1, 2}, {1, 3}, {2, 3}, {1, 2, 3}

2³ = 8

Answer: 8

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting φ and A itself when counting subsets.
  • Writing {1} ∈ A instead of {1} ⊂ A.
  • Adding n(A) + n(B) without subtracting n(A ∩ B).

faq.q: What is the difference between ⊂ and ∈?
faq.a: ∈ links an element to a set (2 ∈ A); ⊂ links a set to a set ({2} ⊂ A).

faq.q: Is φ a subset of every set?
faq.a: Yes. The empty set is a subset of every set, and every set is a subset of itself.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x ∈ Z and −2 ≤ x < 3} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2}.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x = n², n ∈ N and n ≤ 6} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36}.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x is a prime number less than 24} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23}.

items.q: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Which statement is true?
items.e: {1, 5} is a set whose elements are all in A, so it is a subset: {1, 5} ⊂ A ⊂ A. ∈ is used for single elements, as in 5 ∈ A.

items.q: Which set is equal to {x : x is a factor of 10}?
items.e: Equal sets have exactly the same elements: {1, 2, 5, 10}.

items.q: U = {x : x is an integer and 1 ≤ x ≤ 10} and A = {x : x is an even number}. Which statement is true?
items.e: Every element of {2, 6} is in A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, so it is a subset: {2, 6} ⊆ A.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x is a natural number and x² < 70} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8}.

items.q: Which set is equal to {x : x is a factor of 12}?
items.e: Equal sets have exactly the same elements: {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12}.

items.q: Which of these is the empty set?
c: {x : x is an odd number less than 2}
{x : x is an even prime number greater than 2}
items.e: There is no even prime greater than 2, so that set has no elements: ∅. {0} and {∅} each have one element.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x is a natural number and x² < 40} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x is an odd natural number less than 14} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13}.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x = n², n ∈ N and n ≤ 4} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {1, 4, 9, 16}.

items.q: Which set is finite?
c: {x : x is a month of the year}
the set of lines through a point
{x : x ∈ N and x is even}
items.e: {x : x is a month of the year} has a definite number of elements; the others go on without end.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x is a natural number and x² < 50} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7}.

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x is a natural number and x divides 18} in roster form.

items.q: U = {x : x is an integer and 1 ≤ x ≤ 15} and A = {x : x is an even number}. Which statement is true?
items.e: Every element of {2, 4, 12} is in A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14}, so it is a subset: {2, 4, 12} ⊆ A.

items.q: Which of these is the empty set φ?
c: {x : x is an even prime number}
{x : x is a whole number less than 1}
items.e: {x : x² = 4 and x is odd} has no elements. {0} has one element (0), and there is exactly one even prime (2).

items.q: Write the set A = {x : x is a natural number and x divides 20} in roster form.
items.e: List every element that fits the rule, once each: A = {1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20}.

items.q: U = {x : x is an integer and 1 ≤ x ≤ 15} and A = {x : x is a multiple of 3}. Find n(A).
items.e: A = {3, 6, 9, 12, 15}, so n(A) = 5 (the number of elements).

items.q: U = {x : x is an integer and 1 ≤ x ≤ 15} and A = {x : x is a perfect square}. Find n(A).
items.e: A = {1, 4, 9}, so n(A) = 3 (the number of elements).

items.q: Which set is the interval (−4, 5]?
items.e: ( or ) means the end point is not included, [ or ] means it is: {x : −4 < x ≤ 5}.

items.q: Write {x : x ∈ R, 3 < x ≤ 9} as an interval.
items.e: A round bracket leaves the end point out (<) and a square bracket keeps it in (≤): (3, 9].

items.q: If A = {3, 6, 10, 11, 12, 14, 18}, how many elements does the power set P(A) have?
items.e: P(A) is the set of all subsets of A, so n[P(A)] = 27 = 128.

items.q: If A = {s, q, a, r, b, p, c}, how many elements does the power set P(A) have?
items.e: P(A) is the set of all subsets of A, so n[P(A)] = 27 = 128.

items.q: How many subsets does A = {p, s, b, a, r, d, c} have?
items.e: A set with 7 elements has 27 = 128 subsets (including φ and A itself).

items.q: A power set P(A) has 128 elements. How many elements does A have?
If A = {e, a, b}, how many elements does the power set P(A) have?
items.e: P(A) is the set of all subsets of A, so n[P(A)] = 23 = 8.

items.q: If A = {1, 2, 6, 12, 14, 16, 17}, how many elements does the power set P(A) have?

items.q: Which set is the interval [−2, 5)?
items.e: ( or ) means the end point is not included, [ or ] means it is: {x : −2 ≤ x < 5}.

items.q: Write {x : x ∈ R, −2 ≤ x ≤ 3} as an interval.
items.e: A round bracket leaves the end point out (<) and a square bracket keeps it in (≤): [−2, 3].

items.q: How many proper subsets does A = {s, b, c, p, d} have?
items.e: There are 25 = 32 subsets; all except A itself are proper: 31.

items.q: Write {x : x ∈ R, 4 < x < 11} as an interval.
items.e: A round bracket leaves the end point out (<) and a square bracket keeps it in (≤): (4, 11).

items.q: How many subsets does A = {1, 3, 4, 8, 15, 18, 19} have?
items.e: A set with 7 elements has 27 = 128 subsets (including φ and A itself).

items.q: Which set is the interval [5, 12)?
items.e: ( or ) means the end point is not included, [ or ] means it is: {x : 5 ≤ x < 12}.

items.q: U = {x : x is an integer and 1 ≤ x ≤ 12} and A = {x : x is an even number}. List A′.
items.e: A′ is everything in U that is not in A: {1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11}.

items.q: If A = {1, 4, 10, 15, 19}, how many elements does the power set P(A) have?
items.e: P(A) is the set of all subsets of A, so n[P(A)] = 25 = 32.

items.q: Which set is the interval [2, 8)?
items.e: ( or ) means the end point is not included, [ or ] means it is: {x : 2 ≤ x < 8}.

items.q: Which set is shaded in the Venn diagram?
items.e: The shaded part is everything outside A: A′.
B − A keeps the elements of B that are not in A: {7, 8, 10}.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A ∪ B).
items.e: n(A ∪ B) is everything inside either circle: 12 + 2 + 10 = 24.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A′ ∩ B).
items.e: n(A′ ∩ B) is in B but not in A = 14.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A′).
items.e: n(A′) is everything outside A: 11 + 9 = 20.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A′).
items.e: n(A′) is everything outside A: 13 + 2 = 15.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A ∩ B′).
items.e: n(A ∩ B′) is in A but not in B = 6.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A).
items.e: n(A) is everything inside circle A: 14 + 10 = 24.

items.q: Which set is shaded in the Venn diagram?
items.e: The shaded part is everything except the overlap: (A ∩ B)′.

items.q: Which set is shaded in the Venn diagram?
items.e: The shaded part is the overlap of A and B: A ∩ B.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A ∩ B).
items.e: n(A ∩ B) is the overlap only = 5.

items.q: In which region would you put an element that is not in both A and B?
items.e: That description is the set (A ∩ B)′.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A ∩ B).
items.e: n(A ∩ B) is the overlap only = 6.

items.q: Which set is shaded in the Venn diagram?
items.e: The shaded part is everything outside B: B′.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A).
items.e: n(A) is everything inside circle A: 3 + 4 = 7.

items.q: The Venn diagram shows the number of elements in each region. Find n(A ∪ B).
items.e: n(A ∪ B) is everything inside either circle: 7 + 7 + 10 = 24.

items.q: Which set is shaded in the Venn diagram?
items.e: The shaded part is in A but not in B: A ∩ B′.

items.e: n(A ∪ B) = 17 + 18 − 8 = 27 (subtract the overlap once). Neither = 34 − 27 = 7.

items.q: In a class of 44 students, 16 are in the art club, 18 are in the drama club and 2 are in both. How many are in neither?
items.e: n(A ∪ B) = 16 + 18 − 2 = 32 (subtract the overlap once). Neither = 44 − 32 = 12.
